poster_title: Multi-Agent-as-Judge: Aligning LLM-Agent-Based Automated Evaluation with Multi-Dimensional Human Evaluation
authors: Jiaju Chen, Yuxuan Lu, Xiaojie Wang, Huimin Zeng, Jing Huang, Jiri Gesi, Ying Xu, Bingsheng Yao, Dakuo Wang

content: Human work is often collaborative, requiring multi-dimensional evaluations.
Real-world NLP applications need evaluations that consider various stakeholder perspectives.
Traditional metrics often fall short in capturing domain-specific nuances.
MAJ-EVAL constructs structured agent personas from domain-specific research papers.
panels.figure_caption: MAJ-EVAL’s two-step design: Step 1, extract personas; Step 2, in-group debate and aggregation.

content: Agents provide initial evaluations and engage in a free-form debate.
The moderator coordinates the debate, and the aggregator synthesizes the final evaluation.
Evaluated on QAG for children’s storybook reading and medical literature summarization.
Stakeholder groups for QAG: children, parents, and teachers.
Stakeholder groups for medical summarization: care providers, family caregivers, and patients.
MAJ-EVAL achieved better alignment with human ratings compared to traditional metrics.
panels.figure_caption: Spearman’s ρ between evaluation methods and human ratings on StorySparkQA and MSLR-COCHRANE.

content: Debate significantly improved alignment with human ratings for both domains.
panels.figure_caption: Spearman correlations of MAJ-EVAL (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) agents’ scores with human judgments.

content: MAJ-EVAL provides a robust framework for multi-dimensional real-world NLG evaluation.
Significantly improves alignment with human expert ratings, enhancing scalability and consistency.

Fig1.caption: MAJ-EVAL’s two-step design: Step 1, MAJ-EVAL extracts stakeholders’ diverse perspectives from the provided research papers and constructs corresponding personas for the LLM agents. Step 2, agents within the same stakeholder group engage in an in-group debate. An aggregator synthesizes the final evaluation.
Fig1.description: MAJ-EVAL 的两步设计流程图，包含步骤 1 和步骤 2 的详细说明。

Fig2.caption: MAJ-EVAL’s multi-agent-as-judge debate evaluation process (Step 2). Each agent first independently provides an initial evaluation. The moderator then coordinates a free-form debate, allowing agents to discuss and refine their evaluation. Finally, the aggregator synthesizes all agents’ evaluations.
Fig2.description: MAJ-EVAL 的多代理辩论评估过程图，详细描述了步骤 2 的流程。

Fig3.caption: Spearman’s ρ (rank-based correlation) between evaluation methods and human ratings on StorySparkQA (left) and MSLR-COCHRANE (right). Higher values indicate stronger alignments with human judgments. StorySparkQA’s dimensions include Grammar Correctness (GC), Answer Relevancy (AR), Contextuality (CT), and Naturalness (NL).
Fig3.description: 评估方法与人类评分之间的 Spearman 相关性图表，展示了在 StorySparkQA 和 MSLR-COCHRANE 数据集上的表现。

Fig7.caption: Spearman correlations of MAJ-EVAL (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) stakeholder agents’ initial and final scores with human judgments on StorySparkQA (left) and MSLR-COCHRANE (right). Dark blue bars higher than light blue bars indicate improved alignment with human ratings after in-group debate.
Fig7.description: MAJ-EVAL (Claude-3.7-Sonnet) 代理的初始和最终评分与人类评分之间的 Spearman 相关性图表，展示了辩论前后的改进。
